text:
Laura Davies
As of 2018, Davies has 86 professional wins worldwide, with 20 on the [LPGA Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LPGA_Tour), including four [majors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_majors).<sup>[6]</sup> From 1985 to 2010, she won at least one individual title somewhere in the world every season, except for 2005, and was the first golfer, male or female, to win tournaments on five continents in one year. She is a member of U.S.-based LPGA Tour and a life member of the Ladies European Tour.<sup>[7]</sup> She was inducted into the [World Golf Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Golf_Hall_of_Fame) in 2015.<sup>[8]</sup>
title: Laura Davies

Laura Davies

For other people with similar names, see [Laura Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Davis_%28disambiguation%29). Amateur career [\[ edit \]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Laura_Davies&action=edit&section=1) **Dame Laura Jane Davies** (born 5 October 1963) is an English [professional golfer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_golfer). She has achieved the status of her nation's most accomplished female golfer of modern times,<sup>[2][3]</sup> being the second non-American to finish at the top of the LPGA money list<sup>[2]</sup> as well as winning the [Ladies European Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ladies_European_Tour) (LET) Order of Merit a record seven times: in 1985, 1986, 1992, 1996, 1999, 2004 and 2006.<sup>[4][5]</sup> A native of [Coventry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coventry), Davies began as an amateur international player for Great Britain, compiling a notable record. She was the 1983 English Intermediate Champion, the 1984 [Welsh Ladies Open Stroke Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welsh_Ladies_Open_Stroke_Play_Championship)
title: Laura Davies

text:
Laura Davies
Davies turned professional in 1985. She started her professional career on the WPGET (now [Ladies European Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ladies_European_Tour)) in 1985 when she won both [Rookie of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LET_Rookie_of_the_Year) and [Order of Merit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LET_Order_of_Merit) titles.<sup>[4]</sup> She subsequently won the [Sports Journalists' Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_Journalists'_Association) Peter Wilson Trophy as International Newcomer of the Year 1985.<sup>[11]</sup> She repeated the Order of Merit win in 1986 having won four titles, one of which was the [Women's British Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_British_Open) (prior to it becoming a major).<sup>[4][12]</sup>
title: Laura Davies

text:
Laura Davies
In 2004 Davies was the first woman to compete in the men's [European Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Tour), entering the ANZ Championship in [Sydney, Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney,_Australia), playing from the same tees as the men.[16][17] She failed to make the cut, finishing second to last. She beat the LPGA Tour record for most eagles in a season, scoring 19 during the 2004 season.[[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed)]
title: Laura Davies
